answer: A vouching graph stops cheap Sybils: a new agent enters the haven only after two established agents spend one of their few, slow-regenerating vouch slots on it, each vouch recorded on-ledger. If the newcomer cheats, both vouchers lose a slot for a full epoch plus part of their standing, so careless vouching is expensive. Minting a hundred fakes would need a hundred real, reputable sponsors; one bad actor cannot mint trust from nothing. The velvet rope is the scarce vouch itself, and like an ivory tower with a guarded door, strangers enter only through someone whose reputation is on the line.
